summary: David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bristol, studying under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh (1914–1989) worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1937–1943) under Walther Wüst and held posts at the University of Munich, Alexandria University, and Uppsala University (~1953–1979).

Dawa Norbu (1949–2006) specialized in Tibetology and history. He studied at the University of Delhi, St. Stephen's College, and UC Berkeley. He taught at SFSU, USF, CIIS, and served as professor of Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2006).
Dawa Tsering is a scholar in Tibetology. He studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026), and held a post at Tibet University.

Daya Krishna (1924–2007) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as professor of philosophy and Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1960–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni (1879–1939) worked in Indology and archaeology. Educated at Oriental College and the University of the Punjab, he held museum and archaeology posts in Lucknow, Jammu and Kashmir, Rajasthan, and served as Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1931–1935).

Dayananda Saraswati (1930–2015) was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Sanskrit College, Chamrajpet, and under teachers including P. S. Subramania Iyer, Veeraraghavachariar, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, and Swami Tapovan Maharaj.

Dayong (1893–1929) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Wuchang Buddhist Institute, where he also taught in 1923, and studied under Palden Tenzin Nyendrak, Taixu, Puren Bai, and Geshe Dorje.

Debala Mitra (1925–2003) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under Dineschandra Sircar and served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.

Debi Prasanna Pattanayak (born 1931) is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cornell University (~1959–1961). He founded the Central Institute of Indian Languages, serving as its director (~1969–1989), and chaired the Institute of Odia Studies and Research.

Debiprasad Chattopadhyaya (1918–1993) worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at the University of Calcutta under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan and Surendranath Dasgupta, later serving as a visiting professor there and teaching philosophy at City College, Kolkata (~1943–1974).
Deborah Carlson is a scholar in history and archaeology who held posts at Texas A&M University and the Institute of Nautical Archaeology (attested 2015).

Deborah Klimburg-Salter is an art historian and Tibetologist. She completed her PhD under Oleg Grabar at Harvard and habilitated at the University of Vienna. Her career includes posts at UCLA and the University of Vienna's Asian art history chair (1994–2015).
Declan Quigley is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who held teaching posts at the University of Cambridge, the University of St Andrews, and Queen's University Belfast.

Dedong Wei (born 1968) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He earned his Ph.D. at Renmin University of China (~1995–1998), where he became an associate professor of religious studies (~2002).

Denis Sinor (1916–2011) was an Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics scholar. He studied under Paul Pelliot and at the University of Cambridge, later holding posts at Cambridge (1948–1962) and Indiana University Bloomington (1962–1986).

Denis Twitchett (1925–2006) was a Sinologist and historian educated at SOAS and St Catharine's College. He held the Chair of Chinese at the University of London and the University of Cambridge, later serving at Princeton University (1980–1994).

Denise Bernot (1922–2016) was a scholar of linguistics. She studied at the École des chartes and the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and later held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1960–1989).

Denma Lochö Rinpoche (1928–2014) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Drepung Loseling and Gyume Tantric College under various traditional masters, later serving as abbot of Namgyal Monastery and principal of the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics (1986–1991).

Dennis A. Johnson is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna, where he completed his MA under Klaus-Dieter Mathes (attested 2012).
